result:
The proposed answer of 8098 rests on the claim that D(n) = 4 for all n ≥ 3. The solution does not prove this claim; it only asserts it.

- The upper bound says that "longer chains are provably unreachable due to mex constraints", but no argument is given. It only cites checks on a few graph families.
- The mex dynamics should allow longer transients as n grows. A vertex that settles at value k needs neighbors showing 0 through k−1. In a graph with degrees increasing along a chain, vertices can therefore stabilize one after another. That would make the stopping time grow with n rather than stay fixed at 4.
- I did not construct an explicit graph with a transient longer than 4 days. The small simulations I tried either oscillated or converged quickly, so they neither confirm nor refute the claim.

The constant-4 claim is unproven and contradicts the expected growth of the stopping time, so I do not trust the final sum.

VERDICT: REJECT
